I have farmed these 12 mu in Quzhou for 55 years, and I finished high school back in the day, so I can read the county extension handouts and figure out nutrient rates myself. I talk to the input dealer in town and I use the internet at my nephew's house sometimes, but I only change what I do when I see it work on a neighbor's field or mine.

I keep 10 mu in wheat-maize rotation because that is the backbone of my income. The other 2 mu I plant to cotton. Cotton needs more spraying and watering, but when the lint price is over 15 yuan per jin, it pays better than grain.

For my winter wheat already in the ground: I sowed an improved variety, Jimai 26, last October at 25 jin per mu. Last autumn I rotary tilled and put down 80 jin of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer per mu as base. Now at green-up I topdress with 30 jin of urea and irrigate 40 cubic meters per mu. At jointing I put another 20 jin of urea and irrigate again. If May is dry I irrigate once more at grain filling. That comes to about 18 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu. I spray fungicide twice, once at flag leaf and once if I see powdery mildew. I expect 500 kg per mu if late spring brings no frost.

For summer maize on the same 10 mu: right after wheat harvest in early June, I plant hybrid Zhengdan 958. I do not till — I plant no-till straight into the wheat stubble. This saves me diesel and 3 days of labor, and at 73 I need that time. I put 50 jin of 15-15-15 in the seed furrow, then topdress 25 jin urea at big flare stage. I irrigate twice: once after planting if the soil is dry, and once at tasseling. Total nutrients are 15 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, 5 kg potassium per mu. Two pesticide sprays handle the leaf rollers. Expected yield is 550 kg per mu.

For cotton on 2 mu: I plant hybrid Bt cotton. I rotary till in late April and apply 60 jin of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer plus 20 jin of potassium chloride per mu as base. I topdress twice with 15 jin urea each time, at squaring and at flowering. Cotton needs plenty of potassium or the bolls drop before opening. Total is 14 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, 9 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate three times and spray pesticide five times for bollworm, aphids, and red spider mite. I expect 320 kg of seed cotton per mu.

I watch every yuan. Urea costs me about 2.4 yuan per jin, compound fertilizer about 3 yuan per jin. My fertilizer bill is over 4,000 yuan for the whole farm. But last year my neighbor Li cut his wheat fertilizer to save money and lost more than 100 kg per mu — that cost him far more than the fertilizer would have. A bad harvest is a disaster; wasting some fertilizer is just a cost. My wife and I manage the labor ourselves, but I hire a tractor for rotary tilling and a combine for harvest. I need to clear at least 800 yuan profit per mu after all costs, or I am wearing out my body for nothing.
